$comment: Shared input/expected vectors for VfPopover. The TypeScript rules in popover/state.ts run every section; the PHP mirror in packages/razor/src/Support/PopoverState.php runs the sections a server can decide (listed in $serverRules) and deliberately has no method for the others - the trigger key, the flip pair, the arrow offset and the two dismissal predicates are browser decisions a server never makes. The contract of the reference at fd793696, quirks included: Enter and Space toggle and ArrowDown opens; aria-expanded is always written; --top follows the computed placement and there is no --bottom panel modifier; only bottom-end selects the end flip pair; the arrow offset is 0 on an axis missing either number; teleportTo false or null renders in place and anything that is not a string means body; an open popover with closeOnEscape=false still takes an Escape without closing. `null` in `teleportTo` is JSON null; an absent key is `undefined`.

resolvePopoverTriggerKey.$why: ArrowDown opens, and opens again on an open popover; it never closes one.
Keys the trigger leaves to the browser, unprevented.

resolvePopoverContentClasses.$why: The computed placement decides --top, whatever was requested.

resolvePopoverArrowClasses.$why: Anything not starting with top is bottom.

resolvePopoverFlipPlacements.$why: Only bottom-end selects the end pair.

resolvePopoverArrowOffset.$why: A missing base zeroes that axis only.

resolvePopoverTeleport.$why: Explicit null renders in place in Vue. Razor reads a null attribute as not given (its adapter convention) and spells this `false`, so the PHP mirror skips this one vector.
disableTeleport wins over a selector, which is still resolved.

resolvePopoverClosesOnEscape.$why: The entry is still on the stack: the Escape is taken and nothing closes.
